outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the only event bearing on the probability-space version of the problem is an OpenAI catalogue entry released 6 October 2026, claiming a smooth volume-preserving ergodic diffeomorphism of the three-torus with simple Lebesgue spectrum, credited in the repository README to an unreleased internal OpenAI model; the Lean file I could read still ends in 'by sorry', the paper PDF was unreadable to me, and I found no named mathematician engaging with this result. The other window events (Ryzhikov 2024, Abdedou-Fayad-Thouvenot 2024, Ryzhikov 2025-26 items) are neighbouring work that does not settle the bullet.
problem_asks: Whether there exists an ergodic dynamical system with simple Lebesgue spectrum. Unpacked: (1) an ergodic system, which in the bullet is a measure-preserving system; (2) its spectrum, meaning the unitary Koopman operator on the orthocomplement of the constants (mean-zero L2), is of Lebesgue maximal spectral type; (3) multiplicity one, i.e. simple rather than countable or finite multiplicity. The bullet does NOT fix (a) discrete time (a Z-action) versus continuous time (an R-flow, or R^d-actions); (b) finite (probability) measure versus sigma-finite (infinite) measure. Literature readings differ: the Ulam/Scottish-Book formulation is an automorphism of an infinite measure space isomorphic to the line with Lebesgue measure (per search summaries of Ulam's book); the Kanigowski-Lemanczyk 2020 survey and the OpenAI scope note both use the probability-space discrete-time (Z-action) version; flow and R^d versions are separate variants. The Wikipedia link on 'Banach's' goes to the person (Stefan Banach), not to a problem article; 'ergodic system' links to Measure-preserving dynamical system. No Wikipedia article for the problem itself was found.

events.what_happened: J. Mathew and M. G. Nadkarni, 'A measure preserving transformation whose spectrum has Lebesgue component of multiplicity two', Bull. London Math. Soc. 16 (1984) 402-406 (metadata opened at the IAS repository). Per a search summary of the paper (not fully read), it is a Z/2-extension of the dyadic adding machine on a finite measure space with a {0,1}-valued cocycle, whose spectrum has a Lebesgue component of multiplicity two, plus a discrete part. The 2020 survey (section 4.3) cites it as the first finite-multiplicity example.
events.delivers: A measure-preserving discrete-time ergodic transformation on a finite measure space with a Lebesgue component of multiplicity two. Restriction: multiplicity two, not one.
events.remains: Simple (multiplicity one) Lebesgue spectrum for a probability-preserving Z-action: the whole question. Odd multiplicity is also open per the 2020 survey.

checked_by.who: Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society

events.time_since_posted: about 42 years; cited by the 2020 Kanigowski-Lemanczyk survey as giving multiplicity two
events.direction: Neighbouring. It realises multiplicity two on a finite measure space, which the survey treats as the closest finite-measure result, and does not address multiplicity one.
events.object: A rank-one-type Z-action built as a Z/2-extension of the dyadic adding machine (Haar measure on Z_2) by a {0,1}-valued cocycle defined level by level on the tower, per a search summary. Explicit construction; the full text was not read.

events.what_happened: J. Bourgain proved, by Riesz-product techniques, that Ornstein transformations have almost surely singular spectrum, which removed the Ornstein transformations as candidates for simple Lebesgue spectrum. Sources conflict on the date: one search summary gives 1991 (announcement or preprint), another gives Israel J. Math. 84 (1993) 53-63. Bourgain's paper itself was not readable (PDF). Date is taken from secondary sources only.
events.revisions: Journal publication 1993 per a secondary citation; the 1991 date is unverified against a primary source.
events.delivers: Singular spectrum for the Ornstein family of constructions (a negative result about one route, not an existence answer).
events.remains: The whole problem; the Ornstein route is closed.
events.direction: Cuts against one candidate construction for the existence question, and says nothing about other constructions.

events.what_happened: A. El Houcein El Abdalaoui, F. Parreau and A. A. Prikhod'ko, 'A new class of Ornstein transformations with singular spectrum', arXiv math/0502274 (13 Feb 2005; comments say 2004). Abstract (verbatim): 'It is shown that for any family of probability measures in Ornstein type constructions the corresponding transformation has almost surely a singular spectrum. This is a new generalization of Bourgain's theorem, the same result is proved for Rudolph's construction.'
events.delivers: Almost-sure singular spectrum for Ornstein-type and Rudolph-type constructions.
events.remains: The whole problem; these constructions cannot give simple Lebesgue spectrum.
events.direction: Negative about a family of candidate constructions; does not decide existence.

events.what_happened: A. A. Prikhod'ko, 'On flat trigonometric sums and ergodic flow with simple Lebesgue spectrum', arXiv 1002.2808 (15 Feb 2010; one version, no journal reference shown). The fetched abstract says the flatness estimates on a segment are used 'to construct a dynamical system having simple spectrum and Lebesgue spectral type in the class of rank-one flows'.
events.delivers: A rank-one flow (continuous time, R-action) claimed to have simple Lebesgue spectral type. The measure space is not stated in the abstract.
events.remains: The discrete-time Z-action version; whether the measure is a probability measure is not stated.
events.time_since_posted: about 16 years; a journal article with a different title appeared in 2020 (see prikhodko-flows-journal-2020)
events.doubts: Whether this preprint carries the same argument as the 2020 journal paper is not established: the titles differ. Only the abstract was read.
events.direction: Affirmative for flows if the construction holds; neutral for the discrete-time version.
events.object: A rank-one flow built from epsilon-flat trigonometric sums (a Littlewood-type flatness construction), per the abstract. Explicit construction as described; details not read.

events.what_happened: A. A. Prikhod'ko, 'On group actions with simple Lebesgue spectrum', arXiv 1111.0230 (1 Nov 2011; one version). Abstract (verbatim): 'In this paper we propose a construction of measure preserving actions of the group R^d with Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one.'
events.delivers: Measure-preserving R^d actions (continuous time, several parameters) claimed to have Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one.
events.remains: The discrete-time Z-action version; the measure type is not stated in the abstract.
events.doubts: Abstract only read; the construction is not described in the abstract.
events.direction: Affirmative for R^d actions if the construction holds; a different question from Z-actions.
events.object: A construction of measure-preserving R^d actions with Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one; details not read.

events.what_happened: El Houcein El Abdalaoui, 'On the spectral type of some class of rank one flows', arXiv 1205.5543 (v1 24 May 2012; v2 10 Aug 2012, 'submitted for publication'). Abstract (as read): a class of Riesz-product-type measures on the real line is singular, 'which proves the singularity of the spectral types of some class of rank one flows'. The abstract does not mention Banach's problem or Lebesgue spectrum. The comments of arXiv 2007.03684 call 1205.5543 'an earlier announcement of this solution' whose gap is addressed in the 2020 version.
events.delivers: Singular spectral types for some rank-one flows (excludes Lebesgue spectrum for those flows). Does not, on its own abstract, claim a solution of the flow version of Banach's problem; the 2020 arXiv comment says it was an announcement of one.
events.remains: The flow version, if the 2020 comment is taken as describing this paper's claim.
events.doubts: The 2020 arXiv comment on 2007.03684 says this earlier announcement had a gap. I did not find a repair in the 2012 version's abstract.
events.direction: Negative for Lebesgue spectrum for some rank-one flows; the abstract does not claim a positive answer.

events.what_happened: A. A. Prikhod'ko, 'Ergodic automorphisms with simple spectrum characterized by fast correlation decay', arXiv 1301.2795 (13 Jan 2013; v1 only; 5 pages). Abstract: existence of measure-preserving invertible transformations T with simple spectrum and correlation decay of order |k|^(-1/2+eps) for a dense family of functions. The abstract does not claim Lebesgue spectrum.
events.delivers: Discrete-time automorphisms with simple spectrum and a given correlation decay. Not claimed to have Lebesgue spectrum.
events.remains: Lebesgue spectral type, and the whole problem.
events.direction: Neighbouring: simple spectrum without a Lebesgue claim.
events.object: Measure-preserving automorphisms with simple spectrum and prescribed correlation decay; explicit construction per the abstract; details not read.

events.what_happened: E. H. El Abdalaoui and M. G. Nadkarni, 'A non-singular transformation whose spectrum has Lebesgue component of multiplicity one', arXiv 1402.1312 (v1 6 Feb 2014; v2 10 Jul 2014); journal Ergod. Th. Dynam. Sys. 36 (2016) 671-681, DOI 10.1017/etds.2014.85. Abstract: 'an ergodic non-singular map whose unitary operator admits a Lebesgue component of multiplicity one in its spectrum.'
events.delivers: An ergodic non-singular (not measure-preserving) map with a Lebesgue component of multiplicity one.
events.remains: The measure-preserving case, and a pure simple Lebesgue spectrum (the abstract says 'a Lebesgue component').
events.direction: Neighbouring: non-singular rather than measure-preserving. The abstract does not claim a measure-preserving answer.
events.object: An ergodic non-singular map built from partial sums of power series of finite Blaschke products, giving ultraflat polynomials with real coefficients (per a search summary); the abstract gives the multiplicity-one property. Explicit construction.

events.what_happened: El Houcein El Abdalaoui, 'Spectral ergodic Banach problem and flat polynomials', first posted as arXiv 1508.06439 on 26 Aug 2015 and retitled in later versions. Abstract (verbatim): 'We further establish that there is a conservative, ergodic, sigma-finite measure preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum.' It says this 'answer[s] affirmatively a long-standing problem of Banach from the Scottish book'. Version history from the arXiv page: v1 26 Aug 2015; v2 6 Jan 2016; v3 2 Jan 2018; v4 7 Aug 2018; v5 3 Sep 2019; v6 6 Oct 2020; v7 14 Sep 2022; v8 19 Jun 2023 (current). No journal reference shown. Earlier versions used Singer and Sidon sets (search summary only).
events.revisions: v1 26 Aug 2015; v2 6 Jan 2016; v3 2 Jan 2018; v4 7 Aug 2018; v5 3 Sep 2019; v6 6 Oct 2020; v7 14 Sep 2022; v8 19 Jun 2023. The v8 comment says the revision corrects misprints, spelling and grammar.
events.delivers: A conservative, ergodic, sigma-finite measure-preserving transformation (infinite invariant measure) with simple Lebesgue spectrum, built from flat polynomials with coefficients 0 and 1. Restriction: sigma-finite measure, not a probability measure; discrete time.
events.remains: The probability-space discrete-time version (a probability-preserving Z-action with simple Lebesgue spectrum on mean-zero L2), which the 2020 survey and the 2026 OpenAI scope note treat as the problem. Whether the bullet, as worded, already counts a sigma-finite system is for the judging pass.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 years; no journal reference shown on the arXiv page at v8
events.doubts: No specific error found. Signals only: no journal reference after 11 years and 8 versions; the author's later note (2210.15480) says the earlier flatness proof relied on refinements of Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities and deep Carleson-measure and Kadets 1/4 results, and gives a simpler proof; the 2020 survey and Ryzhikov's 2024 notes do not treat this paper as settling the probability version. Full text not read.
events.direction: Affirmative in the sigma-finite setting; the probability (finite-measure) setting is not addressed.
events.object: A conservative ergodic sigma-finite transformation constructed through a sequence of flat polynomials with coefficients 0 and 1 (Newman-type). Per the abstract the result is an existence statement via this construction; the construction's details were not read.

events.direction: Affirmative for flows, per the author's claim.
events.object: A class of Riesz-product-type measures on R realised as spectral types of rank-one flows (per the fetched summary); the flow with simple Lebesgue spectrum is built from these. Construction not read in detail.

Prikhod'ko, 'On ergodic flows with simple Lebesgue spectrum', Matematicheskii Sbornik 211:4 (2020) 123-144; English Sbornik: Mathematics 211:4 (2020) 594-615; DOI 10.4213/sm8147 (10.1070/SM8147). events.what_happened: El Houcein El Abdalaoui, 'L1-flat polynomials and simple Lebesgue spectrum for conservative maps exist: A simple proof', arXiv 2210.15480 (v1 27 Oct 2022; v2 9 Jun 2023, current). Abstract (partial, as fetched): 'we give an example of a conservative ergodic map and flow whose unitary operators admits a simple Lebesgue spectrum.' The v2 comment says a counting argument gives a simpler proof. The text says the earlier flatness result relied on refinements of Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund interpolation and on deep results on Carleson measures and the Kadets 1/4 theorem. No journal reference shown.
events.revisions: v2 9 Jun 2023 (misprints corrected; simpler counting argument).

events.remains: Whether the map is on a probability space is not confirmed, so the probability-space discrete-time version is not established as addressed.
events.direction: Affirmative for conservative maps and flows; setting not confirmed.
events.object: A conservative ergodic map and flow built from L1-flat analytic polynomials with coefficients 0 and 1 on the circle and the real line. Existence via flatness; construction details not read.

events.what_happened: V. V. Ryzhikov, 'Unsolved problems on joinings, multiple mixing, spectrum, and rank', arXiv 2405.03641 (6 May 2024; 19 pages, in Russian). A survey of open problems. It states that a hypothetical automorphism in the class MSJ(2)\MSJ(3) with Lebesgue spectrum, infinite rank and no multiple mixing would, if its spectrum were simple, solve the problems of Banach, Rokhlin and del Junco-Rudolph; the author says such an example 'seems unlikely' and nothing rules it out. The abstract and search extracts were read; the full Russian text was not.
events.delivers: Nothing: a conditional remark that treats Banach's problem as open.
events.remains: All parts of the problem.
events.direction: No result; restates the problem as open.

events.what_happened: V. V. Ryzhikov, 'Spectral properties of dynamical tensor powers, and tensor factorizations of simple Lebesgue spectrum', arXiv 2406.08409 (12 Jun 2024; one version). Abstract paraphrased from the fetch: for every n>0 there is a unitary operator U such that the shift on l2(Z) with simple Lebesgue spectrum is isomorphic to U tensor U^2 tensor ... tensor U^(2^n); and there is an ergodic automorphism T whose symmetric tensor power has simple spectrum while the next power has absolutely continuous spectrum. The introduction calls the case of multiplicity one with Lebesgue maximal type 'Banach's problem'. A related note (Funkts. Anal. Prilozh. 59:2 (2025) 146-148, 'Tensor factorizations of a unitary operator with simple Lebesgue spectrum') appears in search summaries only; not opened.
events.delivers: Factorizations of a unitary operator with simple Lebesgue spectrum into tensor products, and simple (not Lebesgue) spectrum for symmetric tensor powers of an ergodic automorphism. The abstract does not claim an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum.
events.remains: Banach's problem itself, as the author frames it.
events.direction: Neighbouring: unitary-operator factorizations and symmetric powers; no system with simple Lebesgue spectrum is claimed.

events.what_happened: V. V. Ryzhikov, 'On the spectral problems of Kolmogorov and Rokhlin in the class of mixing automorphisms', arXiv 2407.01514 (v1 1 Jul 2024; v2 2 Jul 2024). Abstract summary (fetched): a staircase rank-one construction with r_j ~ j^d, 0<d<0.2, whose spectrum does not have the group property, and whose tensor square has homogeneous spectrum of multiplicity 2. A search summary gives the journal as Russian Math. Surveys 79:6 (2024) 1093-1094 (DOI 10.4213/rm10220); not opened.
events.delivers: Mixing automorphisms without the group property, with homogeneous spectrum of multiplicity 2 for the tensor square. Concerns Kolmogorov's and Rokhlin's problems, not simple Lebesgue spectrum.
events.remains: Banach's problem (not addressed).
events.direction: Neighbouring: multiplicity 2, a different question.

events.what_happened: F. Abdedou, B. Fayad and J.-P. Thouvenot, 'Inducing countable Lebesgue spectrum', arXiv 2409.00396 (31 Aug 2024 per the arXiv page; v1 only). Abstract (verbatim): 'We show that every ergodic dynamical system induces a system with pure Lebesgue spectrum of infinite multiplicity.' It answers a question of de La Rue (1998). Journal: Teor. Veroyatn. Primen. 70(4) (2025) 764-773 (Mathnet record, search summary only).
events.delivers: Induced systems with pure Lebesgue spectrum of infinite multiplicity.
events.remains: Multiplicity one, which is the opposite of what is shown.
events.direction: Neighbouring: a different question (infinite multiplicity rather than one).

events.what_happened: El Houcein El Abdalaoui, 'A generalization of Littlewood's L^alpha flat theorem, alpha>0', arXiv 2509.04212 (4 Sep 2025; v1 only; math.NT with math.DS cross-list). Fetched summary: it proves a generalisation of the L^alpha-flatness criterion for analytic polynomials, states that this confirms the L^alpha-Littlewood conjecture and, as consequences, the L^1-Newman and L^infinity-Erdos conjectures, and says it presents applications in number theory and the spectral theory of dynamical systems. The fetched abstract does not mention +-1 coefficients or Banach's problem. A search snippet claimed a result on +-1 Littlewood polynomials; I could not confirm it from the arXiv abstract and do not rely on it.
events.delivers: An L^alpha-flatness theorem for analytic polynomials (number theory). The dynamical application is not identified in the abstract as read.
events.remains: Banach's problem: no claim about it in the abstract as read.
events.doubts: The dynamical application is not identified in the abstract, so it is not known whether it bears on the Guenais route to multiplicity one (which needs +-1 coefficients). Full text not read.
events.direction: Neighbouring: flatness theorem; the abstract as read does not claim a Banach-problem result.

events.what_happened: S. V. Vereshchagina and V. V. Ryzhikov, 'Explicit Infinite Mixing Automorphisms with Simple Spectra of Symmetric Squares', arXiv 2603.14930 (16 Mar 2026). Fetched summary: mixing ergodic automorphisms of a sigma-finite measure space whose symmetric tensor squares have simple spectra, constructed explicitly in a near-Sidon class; the introduction relates the work to Kolmogorov's and Rokhlin's spectral problems and cites the earlier product T x T multiplicity-two result.
events.revisions: One version seen. A search summary of an HTML version described rank-one constructions, which conflicts with the abstract as fetched.
events.delivers: Sigma-finite mixing automorphisms whose symmetric square has simple spectrum. Not a probability-space result, and the abstract does not claim Lebesgue spectrum for the automorphism itself.
events.remains: Banach's problem, both the probability-space and Lebesgue-spectrum parts.
events.direction: Neighbouring analogue: sigma-finite, and about symmetric squares.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math GitHub repository (catalogue released 6 Oct 2026) lists family 144, 'Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem', with one manuscript, 'A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum' (manuscript folder dated September 23 2026). The scope document (lean/docs/144.md) says Banach's problem 'asks for a probability-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum on its mean-zero L^2 space'. The Lean comparator-challenge file lean/ComparatorChallenges/ThreeTorus.lean (commit adc7f12) has a theorem simple_lebesgue_spectrum : MainConclusion, documented as 'Complete simple Lebesgue spectrum, including the stated consequences', whose proof is 'by sorry'. The claimed content (per the Lean description and the scope note): a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of the three-torus that is ergodic, with a real-valued f whose integer iterates under T are an orthonormal basis of mean-zero L^2, and a unitary identifying the Koopman operator with multiplication by the coordinate function on L^2 of the circle. No human author is named in the sources I could read. The paper PDF could not be read, so its own argument and credit sentence were not seen. Secondary coverage (thendobetter.com, 7 Oct 2026) lists the item as 'produced mainly by an unreleased internal frontier model'; kingy.ai reads family 144 as falling under the common procedure described in the README.
events.revisions: The manuscript folder is dated 2026-09-23 in its name, which may be the authors' date rather than a public posting date; the earliest public appearance I could establish is the catalogue release of 2026-10-06 (community.openai.com post by 'sps' dated 6 Oct; unite.ai 'Published October 6, 2026'; aiweekly gives 7 Oct 03:12 UTC). The README counts 722 manuscripts in 372 families (one fetch read 719). Lean file as read at commit adc7f12; no later commit seen.
events.delivers: If the paper and formal statement hold: a smooth volume-preserving ergodic diffeomorphism of the three-torus (probability measure, discrete time) whose Koopman operator on mean-zero L^2 is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by z on L^2(circle), i.e. simple Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one. This covers the probability-space discrete-time reading in full, if correct.
events.remains: Nothing in the probability-space discrete-time reading, if the claim holds. Unaffected by this event: the sigma-finite Z-action (2015) and the flow version (2010, 2020). Whether the proof is complete is not established: the Lean file as read contains sorry, and no verification is known.

(2) The README says 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations' and 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'; Daily Nous quotes OpenAI's own figure of 42% formalised and a researcher's figure of about 20%. events.direction: Affirmative: claims that an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum exists in the probability-space, discrete-time setting.
events.object: A smooth volume-preserving ergodic diffeomorphism T of the three-torus (the Lean statement uses 'ergodic permutation T of the torus' that is smooth with smooth inverse), with a real-valued f whose orthonormal translates under T^n are dense in mean-zero L^2 (the scope note says they form an orthonormal basis), and a unitary W onto L^2(circle) turning the Koopman action into multiplication by the first Fourier mode. The Lean statement is existential. Whether the construction is explicit or non-constructive is not known from what I could read.

events.what_happened: One manuscript, 'A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its Theorem 1.1 (thm:main) claims that there exist a C^∞ volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of the three-torus T³ (with normalized standard volume) and a real function f in the mean-zero space L²_0(T³) such that the bilateral orbit {f∘Tⁿ : n∈Z} is an orthonormal basis of all of L²_0. The same theorem derives that T is ergodic and that the Koopman operator U_T on L²_0 is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by w on L²(S¹, m), which is simple Lebesgue spectrum. The proof is an inductive limit. It builds smooth volume-preserving maps S_n, which are twists (θ,u,a) ↦ (θ+φ(u),u,a) reached through volume-preserving coordinate passages, with observables f_n whose spectral density is made exactly one by a whitening step (§5). The sequence converges in C^∞ to T, and completeness of the orbit comes from approximating a dense family of test functions by Laurent polynomials in U applied to f_n. Section 6 (Corollary 'dynamical-profile') adds mixing, zero entropy and vanishing Lyapunov exponents. Its mixing of order k≥3 depends on a separate OpenAI preprint, 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (cited as MultipleMixing2026, Theorem 1.1), which I did not read. The abstract says: 'We solve the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem in smooth dynamics.'
events.delivers: Existence of an ergodic, probability-preserving, discrete-time (Z-action) system with simple Lebesgue spectrum on its mean-zero L² space. The example is a smooth (C^∞) volume-preserving diffeomorphism of T³ with standard volume. Simple means multiplicity one, and Lebesgue means the spectral type is Haar measure on the circle; both are obtained from one cyclic orbit. The manuscript states its own scope. The abstract restricts the claim to 'the probability-preserving form', and §1 says that formulation is 'distinct from the historical real-line question recorded by Ulam and attributed to Banach'. So the claim is not offered for the infinite-measure line version. The manuscript defines the probability-preserving form in §1 as the Koopman operator on the orthogonal complement of the constants. It does not restate the list's bullet word for word, so this is a reading of that bullet, and the family matches the reading that the problem_asks note names for finite measure and Z-actions. The generator f is only required to lie in L² (real, centered, norm one), so the observable is not smooth. The smoothness claim is for T alone.
events.remains: If the claim is correct, the probability-preserving, discrete-time reading is answered by existence, and parts (1)–(3) of problem_asks are met under that reading. Left open by this family: the infinite-measure (Ulam, real-line) reading, which the manuscript explicitly sets aside; continuous time (flows and R^d actions), which §1 discusses only through other results (Prikhod'ko, Fayad–Forni–Kanigowski, Abdedou–Fayad–Kessi) without settling the simple-Lebesgue question for flows; and any class of examples other than C^∞ volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of T³ (other manifolds, other regularity classes, analytic maps).

machine_checked.scope: Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem asks for a probability-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum on its mean-zero $L^2$ space. The formalization constructs a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the three-torus with this property. It gives a real-valued cyclic vector whose integer iterates form an orthonormal basis of the entire mean-zero space, and an isometric identification under which the Koopman operator becomes multiplication by the coordinate function on the circle. The transformation is also ergodic.

events.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched, hedged or deferred. A search for 'sketch', 'omit', 'routine' and 'left to' found nothing of the kind. The argument is long and compressed, and each stage is a sequence of choices of the form 'arbitrarily small after the earlier finite data are fixed'. The key inputs are the passage lemma (§2), the signal lemma (§3), and the prediction proposition and finite phase-test lemma (§4). I read their statements and only selected passages, so my account of them rests mainly on their statements. The abstract's 'solve' is qualified to the probability-preserving form in the abstract itself, but the title has no such qualification. The mixing corollary's order-≥3 mixing depends on the separate MultipleMixing2026 preprint. Its zero-entropy step uses Rokhlin's finite-multiplicity theorem, and its vanishing-exponent step uses Pesin's formula as stated by Mañé. These are cited rather than proved here, and they are not needed for the spectral claim itself. I found no inconsistency between the abstract and Theorem 1.1.

disputes.summary: Which problem is Banach's: the Ulam/Scottish-Book line (sigma-finite measure, Lebesgue measure on the line; El Abdalaoui 2015 claims to answer it), the probability-space discrete-time version (the Kanigowski-Lemanczyk 2020 survey, section 4.3, calls the Z-action multiplicity-one question open; the OpenAI scope note uses this version), or the flow and R^d variants (Prikhod'ko and El Abdalaoui 2010-2020). The bullet does not choose.

Matematicheskii Sbornik 211:4 (2020), pp. 123-144 (Sbornik: Mathematics 211:4, pp. 594-615). The arXiv comments on 2007.03684 say El Abdalaoui's paper was republished at these pages. The journal record (journals.rcsi.science, DOI 10.4213/sm8147) names A. A. Prikhod'ko as the sole author of 'On ergodic flows with simple Lebesgue spectrum'. One of the two attributions is wrong, and I could not check the Mathnet page directly (connection refused).

arXiv 2007.03684 (comments) calls arXiv 1205.5543 'an earlier announcement of this solution' whose gap is addressed in the 2020 version. The 1205.5543 abstract, as read, claims singular spectral types for some rank-one flows and does not mention Banach's problem or Lebesgue spectrum.

The OpenAI README (second fetch) reads '722 manuscripts organized into 372 families'; the first fetch read '719 manuscripts in 372 families', and press (Daily Nous quoting 719; community and other coverage 722) differs. Not resolved; this affects the release count, not the family-144 entry.

summary: The bullet asks for 'an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum' without fixing discrete or continuous time, or finite or sigma-finite measure, so the record has to be read against several versions. The Wikipedia bullet is confirmed: 'Banach's problem - is there an ergodic system with simple Lebesgue spectrum?', with the link on 'Banach's' pointing to Stefan Banach and 'ergodic system' to Measure-preserving dynamical system; I found no problem article. Before the window: El Abdalaoui's arXiv 1508.06439 (26 Aug 2015, v8 June 2023, no journal reference shown) claims a conservative ergodic sigma-finite measure-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum and calls it an affirmative answer to Banach's Scottish-Book problem; Prikhod'ko's flow results (arXiv 1002.2808 in 2010; Mat. Sb. 211:4 (2020), whose abstract claims ergodic flows with a probability measure and Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one); and El Abdalaoui's flow claim in arXiv 2007.03684 (2020), whose attribution conflicts with the journal record. The probability-space discrete-time version, which is the reading the release and the specialist survey use, was stated as open in Kanigowski and Lemanczyk's 2020 survey (section 4.3, quoted: 'no example of a Koopman representation with Lebesgue spectrum of finite multiplicity is known'; 'still an open question remains whether for Z one can find a Koopman representation with the Lebesgue component of multiplicity 1'), and Ryzhikov's 2024 notes (arXiv 2405.03641) treat it as open. Other pre-window results found are neighbouring: Mathew-Nadkarni 1984 (multiplicity two), Ornstein-route negatives (Bourgain 1991/1993 secondary; Abdalaoui-Parreau-Prikhod'ko 2005), a non-singular multiplicity-one map (El Abdalaoui-Nadkarni 2014). Window events (since 26 Jan 2024) other than the OpenAI entry are neighbouring and do not settle the bullet: Ryzhikov 2024 (open-problems survey; tensor powers; Kolmogorov/Rokhlin), Abdedou-Fayad-Thouvenot 2024 (infinite multiplicity), El Abdalaoui 2025 (L^alpha flatness; abstract does not mention Banach's problem or +-1 coefficients; a search summary's claim about +-1 polynomials was not confirmed), and Vereshchagina-Ryzhikov 2026 (sigma-finite symmetric squares). The one window event on the probability-space version is OpenAI's openai/math family 144, released 6 Oct 2026: a claimed smooth volume-preserving ergodic diffeomorphism of the three-torus with simple Lebesgue spectrum, stated in a Lean comparator-challenge file whose main theorem's proof is 'by sorry' at commit adc7f12 (read through a summarising fetch). The README credits the vast majority of the 722 manuscripts to 'an unreleased internal OpenAI model' under one fixed procedure, with a stated average of three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute per result; family 144 is not among the named exceptions, but the paper's own credit sentence was not readable (the PDF returned binary). I found no named mathematician, journal, arXiv posting or expert comment specific to this result. General reactions (Tao, Wood, Sutherland, Litt, Easwaran, Michel) concern the release. AI search: across the Banach-specific sources I found no AI involvement except this release; the only other 2026 AI-related dynamics item I saw in a search summary (arXiv 2608.20105, an AI-discovered fast dynamo on T^3) is not about this problem, and I did not open it. Close calls: (a) the bullet's scope (if any sigma-finite system counts, El Abdalaoui 2015 already answers the bullet as worded, and the 2026 claim is a stronger probability-space result); (b) the date (folder name 23 Sept 2026; public catalogue release 6 Oct 2026; I used 6 Oct because that is the earliest public appearance I could establish); (c) the Mat. Sb. attribution; (d) the 719/722 manuscript count. Not checked: the 1966 Kirillov scepticism ('there are grounds for thinking that such examples do not exist', seen only in a search summary); the Scottish-Book problem number (Kadets's Problem 106 concerns series, so it is not this problem); the journal status of 1508.06439; the Lemanczyk 2019 survey's open-problem list (search snippet only).
competing_reading: (1) The problem as worded was answered before the window: El Abdalaoui's 2015 sigma-finite result gives an ergodic measure-preserving system with simple Lebesgue spectrum, and the 2020 flow results do the same for flows, so the 2026 OpenAI claim is a strengthening to the probability-space discrete-time case rather than the first resolution. (2) The 2026 claim is not yet a settlement of any reading: its formal theorem is sorry in the file I read, its paper was not read, and no specialist has engaged; on that view nothing in the window has settled even the probability-space version, and the record's 'open' status stands until verification. (3) On the probability-space reading, which the 2020 survey and the release both use, the 2026 claim is the first positive answer if it holds, and it was produced by an unreleased internal model.
what_would_settle_it: (a) The paper's own text (the repository's paper PDF) read directly, including its credit sentence and proof, and whether it names a model. (b) A sorry-free Lean proof of simple_lebesgue_spectrum (or a comparator-accepted solution), plus a check that MainConclusion matches the stated mathematical claim. (c) Expert verification by ergodic theorists (publicly), or an arXiv or journal posting with referees. (d) Whether the bullet means the probability-space Z-action version or any ergodic system: this decides whether El Abdalaoui 2015 already answers it. (e) The journal status of arXiv 1508.06439 and whether any 2024-2026 survey still lists the probability version as open. (f) The journal of record for Mat. Sb. 211:4 (pp. 123-144): Prikhod'ko, or El Abdalaoui as the arXiv comment says. (g) The text of arXiv 1205.5543's claimed flow result and the gap noted in arXiv 2007.03684.

event.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math GitHub repository (catalogue released 6 Oct 2026) lists family 144, 'Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem', with one manuscript, 'A smooth three-torus diffeomorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum' (manuscript folder dated September 23 2026). The scope document (lean/docs/144.md) says Banach's problem 'asks for a probability-preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum on its mean-zero L^2 space'. The Lean comparator-challenge file lean/ComparatorChallenges/ThreeTorus.lean (commit adc7f12) has a theorem simple_lebesgue_spectrum : MainConclusion, documented as 'Complete simple Lebesgue spectrum, including the stated consequences', whose proof is 'by sorry'. The claimed content (per the Lean description and the scope note): a smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism T of the three-torus that is ergodic, with a real-valued f whose integer iterates under T are an orthonormal basis of mean-zero L^2, and a unitary identifying the Koopman operator with multiplication by the coordinate function on L^2 of the circle. No human author is named in the sources I could read. The paper PDF could not be read, so its own argument and credit sentence were not seen. Secondary coverage (thendobetter.com, 7 Oct 2026) lists the item as 'produced mainly by an unreleased internal frontier model'; kingy.ai reads family 144 as falling under the common procedure described in the README.
event.revisions: The manuscript folder is dated 2026-09-23 in its name, which may be the authors' date rather than a public posting date; the earliest public appearance I could establish is the catalogue release of 2026-10-06 (community.openai.com post by 'sps' dated 6 Oct; unite.ai 'Published October 6, 2026'; aiweekly gives 7 Oct 03:12 UTC). The README counts 722 manuscripts in 372 families (one fetch read 719). Lean file as read at commit adc7f12; no later commit seen.
event.delivers: If the paper and formal statement hold: a smooth volume-preserving ergodic diffeomorphism of the three-torus (probability measure, discrete time) whose Koopman operator on mean-zero L^2 is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by z on L^2(circle), i.e. simple Lebesgue spectrum of multiplicity one. This covers the probability-space discrete-time reading in full, if correct.
event.remains: Nothing in the probability-space discrete-time reading, if the claim holds. Unaffected by this event: the sigma-finite Z-action (2015) and the flow version (2010, 2020). Whether the proof is complete is not established: the Lean file as read contains sorry, and no verification is known.

judgement.why: I read the statement the way its link to 'Measure-preserving dynamical system' and the specialist literature (Kanigowski-Lemanczyk 2020, Ryzhikov 2024) read it: an ergodic, probability-preserving Z-action whose Koopman operator on mean-zero L2 has simple Lebesgue spectrum. On that reading, each pre-snapshot affirmative result is a changed question (variant): sigma-finite measure (El Abdalaoui 2015/2022), flows or R^d actions (Prikhod'ko 2010/2011/2020, El Abdalaoui 2020), non-singular maps (2014). Multiplicity-two and infinite-multiplicity results are also variants. Negative results about particular constructions, and surveys, are scope none. The OpenAI manuscript claims exactly this probability-preserving Z-action, as an existence theorem: a C^inf volume-preserving diffeomorphism of T^3 with a cyclic vector whose orbit is an orthonormal basis of L2_0. That answers the existence question in full if it is correct, so the scope is whole. The limit map is non-explicit, so it is not checkable; nobody has reviewed it, the Lean main theorem was seen as 'by sorry', so it is unreviewed. It is credible, because no specific error has been identified and only 8 days have passed. The object is a witness. The AI role is generated on the README's procedure statement, and the family is not among the named exceptions. The two OpenAI entries describe one release; I scored them identically.
judgement.doubts: Close call on scope: the bullet does not fix the measure or the time group. If a sigma-finite or flow system counts, El Abdalaoui 2015 or Prikhod'ko 2020 (journal-published) would already answer the bullet before the snapshot. I chose the probability-preserving Z-action reading, following the link target and the specialist surveys. The AI credit rests on the README's general statement; the manuscript's own credit sentence was not read. The two OpenAI events duplicate one release.
